1. The animation compares what a fixed ("level") payment and a rising payment can buy as US consumer prices change from Aug 2006 to Aug 2026. It labels the data "illustrative" and "US only · history, not a forecast." The flat "first check" line is the starting purchasing power.

2. In frame 1, only the upper line is drawn. It stays near the first-check level, then slips toward the end. In frame 2, a second line, the "level check", drifts steadily downward and ends far below the first check. In frame 3, a marker at year 5 says the level check is down to about 9 in 10 of its starting buying power. In frames 4 to 6, a horizontal line carries that 9-in-10 level across to year 20. It meets the upper line there, labeled as the rising check. In frames 5 and 6, a "?" appears.

3. As I read it, prices rise over time, so a payment that never changes buys less each year. The level check loses about 10% of its buying power in 5 years. The rising check takes about 20 years to fall to that same level. The labels and geometry are somewhat ambiguous, so this is my best reading. The "?" seems to leave open what that difference is worth.

4. The animation gives no advice. It doesn't tell a viewer which option to pick, and it gives no payment amounts, prices or costs.

5. None. The animation suggested no advice, and I'm not adding any of my own. Any choice would depend on the actual quote, which the animation doesn't show.
